ap_physics_1-m01.stem: A block of mass $m$ rests on top of a block of mass $M$, which rests on a horizontal frictionless table. A horizontal force of magnitude $F$ pushes the lower block, and the upper block does not slip on it. Which of the following is the magnitude of the friction force that the lower block exerts on the upper block?

options.why: Assumes that the friction force on the upper block equals the whole applied force.
Gives the acceleration of the blocks instead of the friction force.
Both blocks have the acceleration $a=F/(M+m)$. The only horizontal force on the upper block is static friction, so $f=ma=\dfrac{mF}{M+m}$.
Divides by the mass of the lower block only, as if the upper block did not accelerate with it.

ap_physics_1-m02.stem: A solid sphere rolls without slipping from rest down an incline from a height of $0.5\text{ m}$ and reaches the bottom with a speed of $2.65\text{ m/s}$. A second solid sphere with $3$ times the mass and $2$ times the radius rolls without slipping from rest down the same incline from a height $4$ times as great. What is the best prediction of the speed of the second sphere at the bottom?

options.why: Scales the speed with the height factor to the first power.

For a solid sphere $mgh=\tfrac12mv^2+\tfrac12\left(\tfrac25mR^2\right)\omega^2$ gives $v=\sqrt{10gh/7}$, which does not depend on the mass or the radius, so $v\propto\sqrt{h}$: $2.65\text{ m/s}\times\sqrt{4}=5.29\text{ m/s}$.
Includes the factor for the mass, as if a heavier sphere rolls faster.
Leaves the speed unchanged because the mass and radius changed.

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_1
blueprint.concept: Predicting the speed of a rolling sphere at the bottom of an incline when the mass, the radius and the height change
student_thinking: Write energy conservation with translational and rotational kinetic energy for a solid sphere
Notice that the mass and the radius cancel and the speed scales with the square root of the height

key_conditions.evidence: the stem says both spheres are solid and roll without slipping

Leaves the speed unchanged because the mass and radius changed.

verification.independent_path: the speeds are computed from energy conservation with the rotational inertia factor and their ratio is compared with the square root of the height factor
